主体设定：<Subject 1> 是 <Picture 1> 画面左侧的男性，保留束起的发髻、短须与沉静的脸，宽大厚重、袍摆拖地的深色长袍，腰间一长一短两柄刀，右手长刀；<Subject 2> 是 <Picture 1> 画面右侧的男性，保留束起的发髻与清瘦的脸，深色衣装外肩披边缘毛糙的粗布披风，刀柄垂着绳穗，右手长刀；<Subject 3> 是 <Picture 1> 中的竹林空地：湿透的深色石板地、贴地的雾、两侧密集竹林。动作中两人的身份与整套服装不变。

概述：[参考生成] 风从左吹向右的竹林空地上，<Subject 1> 以长刀大弧守住身前一整圈刀圈，一步一刀向前压；<Subject 2> 要破开这道刀圈、贴进他一步之内。前者斩倒竹子封住后者的路线，后者借倒竹与弯竹的回弹两次突入，最后用刀柄撞落对方的长刀，两人在新位置继续交锋。

视觉：写实电影质感，低饱和青灰冷调，雾、湿地反光与竹林纵深层层分明，冷白天光从竹林顶端漫下勾出两人轮廓。两人都束发、衣着深色，以短须与厚袍、清瘦与披风区分，换位后也不混淆。刀刀相撞的火星是全片唯一的暖色，只在接触点一闪即灭，不是光效；竹子倒下的方向由斩击方向决定。空地右侧竹林边那根最粗的竹竿是固定地标，全片位置不变。无血，画面无文字水印。

[Shot 1] 贴地低位广景，从右侧竹林边穿过前景竹竿看向空地，雾被风拉成贴地的带子。<Subject 1> 从左侧压来，长刀一记大弧扫满身前；<Subject 2> 从右侧低身冲进，刀尖直取他的前膝。大弧的刀背砸在 <Subject 2> 刀身中段，把刀尖压进积水、划出一道水线，火星与水花同时炸起，<Subject 2> 被弹回刀圈外。他借回弹再冲，<Subject 1> 不砍人，横刀齐腰斩断他前方两根竹竿，竹子一前一后横倒封路；<Subject 2> 贴着湿石板从第一根竹子下方滑过，水花扇形铺开，第二根正从他头顶压下。

[Shot 2] 00:05.000 切绕行的全身机位，刚倒下的竹竿仍横在两人之间，那根最粗的竹竿在画面右侧。<Subject 2> 一脚蹬上正在倒下的竹竿，借倾倒变向跃起，从高处斜劈；<Subject 1> 双手横刀架在头顶，两刀相交处迸出火星，这一劈的分量把他压得单膝砸进积水。他借最低的重心整身一拧，肩膀由下往上撞进 <Subject 2> 胸口；<Subject 2> 倒飞出去，后背撞上那根最粗的竹竿，竹子整根弯到极限、竹叶倾泻。竹子回弹，把他整个人弹回来，正迎上 <Subject 1> 刚抡满的第二记大弧：两刀正撞，<Subject 2> 的刀几乎脱手，手腕被砸得向后折，身体被带着转了半圈。<Subject 1> 的长刀停在弧尾，厚袍慢半拍向后甩开，持刀手的另一侧露出空门。

[Shot 3] 00:10.000 切更低、更广的视角，地上横着被斩倒的竹竿与一道道水痕。<Subject 2> 顺着这半圈旋转压到最低，从还没收回的长刀下方钻进刀圈，贴到 <Subject 1> 持刀手的另一侧，两人左右换位。他反手用刀柄尾端猛撞长刀的护手根部：刀先被撞得一偏，才从 <Subject 1> 右手脱出，翻转着甩过 <Subject 2> 肩头，扎进那根最粗的竹竿，刀身震颤，竹叶纷落。<Subject 1> 左手已拔出腰间短刀横在身前，<Subject 2> 后撤半步沉低，刀尖对准他，两人随即再次移动脚步。扎在竹上的长刀保留在身后，两人的面孔、衣装与新的站位都清楚。

声音：风穿竹林的持续呼啸与竹叶沙沙声，湿石板上的脚步与滑行水声，长刀大弧沉厚的破风、快刀尖细的哨音，刀刀相撞的金属炸响，竹竿断裂的脆响与弯竹回弹的弹响，刀柄撞上护手的一记钝响，长刀扎进竹竿后的余颤。无对白或喊招式名。配乐以低沉太鼓与尺八渐紧，仅在长刀被撞脱手时加入一次重鼓。

<Picture 1> = Li Xiang character three-view sheet: an East Asian man shown in multiple orthographic views (front, three-quarter, side, back), grey-streaked hair in a topknot secured by a wooden hairpin, wearing a brown leather armored vest over a blue inner robe and blue trousers, a red cloth belt at the waist, black boots, a small wooden talisman hanging at the hip. His face, hair, build and costume are anchored to this three-view sheet.
<Picture 2> = the courtyard, camera side A, front side: a wide stone-paved courtyard laid in large grey slabs and scattered with dry leaves, in front of a traditional hall with a grey-tile hip-and-gable roof, a long row of wooden lattice doors and windows along its front, red lanterns hanging in rows under the eaves on both sides, a raised stone terrace with carved stone statues flanking its steps, and mature trees framing the left and right edges; strong golden backlight with visible sun rays streaming through the trees from behind the hall, long shadows raking toward the camera. Only the architecture, the paving, the light and the composition are taken from it.
<Picture 3> = the courtyard, camera side B, reverse side: the same courtyard and the same hall seen from the opposite camera side, the hall receding behind the performer with its grey-tile roof, wooden lattice front and red lanterns under the eaves, the stone terrace and carved statue at its entrance, trees crowding both edges with the sun high and burning through the foliage on the right, dry leaves and sparse dry grass on the paving. Only the architecture, the paving, the light and the composition are taken from it.
<Video 1> = the motion reference for segment C : Li Xiang practising the Dugu Nine Swords aerial work and the sword strikes — repeated push-off spins, a sword tip driven point-down into the stone paving with the blade flexing, the blade springing back, and a flying blade striking the ground. Only the motion rhythm, the body mechanics, the blade path and the camera movement are taken from this video.
<Subject 1> = Li Xiang (S1): an East Asian man, grey-streaked hair in a topknot with a wooden hairpin, brown leather armored vest over a blue inner robe and blue trousers, red cloth belt, black boots, a wooden talisman at the hip, holding one straight double-edged jian sword with a dark hilt. He has exactly one head, two arms, two legs and two hands, and he holds one sword and only one sword. He has no lines and never speaks.
CRITICAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE TWO SCENE STILLS: <Picture 2> and <Picture 3> show the same one man standing in the same one courtyard, and differ only in which side of him the camera is on, front side and reverse side. That man is <Subject 1>, seen from the front in <Picture 2> and from behind in <Picture 3>. He is one person, not two. His figure in both stills serves as a pose and framing guide only and is fully replaced by <Subject 1>; never render the figure from <Picture 2> and the figure from <Picture 3> as two separate people standing together, and never render either of them beside <Subject 1>.
summary:
[reference generation] From one character three-view sheet, two camera sides of the same courtyard, and one motion reference video, generate an approximately 7.9-second realistic wuxia sword-practice video in a 21:9 landscape frame, the Dugu Nine Swords segment C. One man, Li Xiang, alone in an entirely empty courtyard: he pushes off into a single aerial flip, drops into ground-level low sword work and lifts the blade, goes up into another single flip, drives the point vertically down into the stone paving so the blade flexes into a drawn bow and trembles under the load, the blade springs back and catapults him into a twisting aerial flip, the released blade strikes the paving point-first and throws a single spark, and he lands and settles. Motion rhythm and camera follow <Video 1>. This is solo practice: there is no opponent, no sparring partner, no bystander and no second person, the frame never holds two figures, and this video contains exactly one sword.

<Picture 2>: partially_preserved - only the architecture, the grey-tile roof, the lattice front, the rows of red lanterns, the stone terrace and statues, the slab paving, the trees and the golden backlit sun rays are carried over as the front-side camera environment; the man standing in the reference is the same single person as <Subject 1> and is never rendered as an additional character.
<Picture 3>: partially_preserved - only the architecture, the receding hall, the lanterns, the stone terrace and statue, the foliage-framed edges, the high right-hand sun and the leaf-strewn paving are carried over as the reverse-side camera environment of the same courtyard; the man standing in the reference is the same single person as <Subject 1> and is never rendered as an additional character.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved - only the motion rhythm, the body mechanics, the blade path and the camera movement are carried over; the performer's likeness is replaced entirely by <Subject 1>, and the performer is never rendered as a separate figure.
detailed_description:
The visual style is live-action cinematic wuxia, realistic, 21:9 landscape frame, golden morning backlight with long shadows across a large stone-paved courtyard in front of a grey-tile-roofed hall hung with red lanterns, crisp clean air, normal undistorted human anatomy, one single performer alone in an entirely empty courtyard, no other person enters the frame at any moment, no opponent, no sparring partner, no bystander, no onlooker, no disciple, no servant, no figure standing in the background, no duplicate of the character; the blade is a real physical steel blade with no magical glow, no energy beams and no particle trails; no on-screen text, no subtitles, no watermarks, no logos, no frame numbers, no deformed hands, no extra fingers, no duplicated blade. The motion rhythm and camera movement follow <Video 1>; the [Shot] blocks below are structural cues only; each aerial spin is a single revolution with a landing or a ground beat between revolutions, never a continuous chain; the blade stays the same single straight double-edged jian with a dark hilt from the first frame to the last and is never duplicated, never bent except for the flex in [Shot 4], and never dissolving; in [Shot 4] the blade is allowed and required to flex into a deep bow and then spring back straight. The two camera sides of <Picture 2> and <Picture 3> belong to one single courtyard and simply give the sequence its front and reverse angles, and the one man standing in each of those stills is <Subject 1> himself, one person photographed from two sides, never two men. [Segment-level state lock: STATE LOCKED - SOLO LOCKED, exactly one human being in the frame from the first frame to the last and the courtyard entirely empty behind him; LI XIANG'S OUTFIT LOCKED, red sash SASH LOCKED, flaring with his momentum; ONE SWORD LOCKED, a single straight double-edged jian with a dark hilt, in his hand from the first frame through [Shot 5], falling alone for the single strike in [Shot 6], and back in his one hand in [Shot 7].]
[Shot 1] At 00:00.000, a wide tracking shot on the front side — purpose: the opening aerial flip. Carrying on from the previous segment, Li Xiang drives off the ground into one aerial flip with the sword in one hand, his body opening out in the air. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2> as the front side, the hall and its lantern rows behind him; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution only. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 2] At 00:01.400, a medium shot on the reverse side — purpose: ground-level low sword work, lifting the blade. Coming down out of the flip, he sinks into low ground-level sword work and lifts the blade to gather the next movement. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3> as the reverse side, the hall receding behind him; character <Picture 1>. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 3] At 00:02.600, a medium orbiting shot on the front side — purpose: a second aerial flip. From the lift he goes up into another aerial flip, his body fully extended in the air. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2>; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution, with a landing between this flip and the one before. [Solo lock: one figure in frame; the blade stays in his hand through the revolution.]
[Shot 4] At 00:04.100, an extreme close-up from a ground-skimming low camera — purpose: the signature beat, sword point driven into the paving and the blade flexing into a drawn bow. Coming down out of the flip he drives the blade down and the point bites vertically into the grey stone slab; the frame is tight on the blade and the point, the steel flexing into a deep bow like a fully drawn bowstring, the blade trembling under the load, the point nailed into the stone and not coming out. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; lighting and paving from <Picture 3>; character <Picture 1>. The core of this beat is the deep bow-shaped flex of the blade, the point straight down, the sword never breaking. [Solo lock: only his one hand on the hilt and the one blade in frame; nobody else anywhere.]
[Shot 5] At 00:05.000, a wide low-angle shot on the reverse side — purpose: the blade springs back and catapults him into a twisting aerial flip. With the flex fully loaded, the bowed blade snaps back like a released bowstring and throws him up off the ground, his body twisting into an aerial flip and opening out in the air with the sun blazing through the foliage behind him. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3> as the reverse side, the high right-hand sun behind him; character <Picture 1>. Launched by the blade's rebound, one single twisting revolution, a crisp landing. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 6] At 00:06.100, a medium close shot with the camera low and locked on the blade — purpose: the released blade strikes the paving and throws a single spark. The blade has left his hand and drops alone, point-first, into the grey stone paving; the point bites the stone, a single spark jumps at the point of impact, and the blade stands there bright and straight. Nothing holds it: no hand grips it, no hand throws it, no hand steers it, and there is no other person in this courtyard who could be holding it. Motion and blade path follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2>; character <Picture 1>. One strike only, one single spark, the blade perfectly straight at the moment of impact. [Solo lock: the only thing moving in the frame is this one blade landing in an empty courtyard.]
[Shot 7] At 00:06.400, a wide tracking shot on the reverse side — purpose: continued air work and the closing settle. From the strike he goes up into one more aerial flip and then lands and settles, his robes falling quiet around him. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3>; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution, a crisp landing. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]

One man, Li Xiang, alone in an entirely empty courtyard: he pushes off into a single aerial flip, drops into ground-level low sword work and lifts the blade, goes up into another single flip, drives the point vertically down into the stone paving so the blade flexes into a drawn bow and trembles under the load, the blade springs back and catapults him into a twisting aerial flip, the released blade strikes the paving point-first and throws a single spark, and he lands and settles. Motion rhythm and camera follow <Video 1>. This is solo practice: there is no opponent, no sparring partner, no bystander and no second person, the frame never holds two figures, and this video contains exactly one sword.
retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - Li Xiang's face, hair, costume and silhouette are preserved from <Picture 1> continuously from the first frame to the last, and he remains the only person in frame throughout.
<Picture 2>: partially_preserved - only the architecture, the grey-tile roof, the lattice front, the rows of red lanterns, the stone terrace and statues, the slab paving, the trees and the golden backlit sun rays are carried over as the front-side camera environment; the man standing in the reference is the same single person as <Subject 1> and is never rendered as an additional character.
<Picture 3>: partially_preserved - only the architecture, the receding hall, the lanterns, the stone terrace and statue, the foliage-framed edges, the high right-hand sun and the leaf-strewn paving are carried over as the reverse-side camera environment of the same courtyard; the man standing in the reference is the same single person as <Subject 1> and is never rendered as an additional character.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved - only the motion rhythm, the body mechanics, the blade path and the camera movement are carried over; the performer's likeness is replaced entirely by <Subject 1>, and the performer is never rendered as a separate figure.
detailed_description:
The visual style is live-action cinematic wuxia, realistic, 21:9 landscape frame, golden morning backlight with long shadows across a large stone-paved courtyard in front of a grey-tile-roofed hall hung with red lanterns, crisp clean air, normal undistorted human anatomy, one single performer alone in an entirely empty courtyard, no other person enters the frame at any moment, no opponent, no sparring partner, no bystander, no onlooker, no disciple, no servant, no figure standing in the background, no duplicate of the character; the blade is a real physical steel blade with no magical glow, no energy beams and no particle trails; no on-screen text, no subtitles, no watermarks, no logos, no frame numbers, no deformed hands, no extra fingers, no duplicated blade. The motion rhythm and camera movement follow <Video 1>; the [Shot] blocks below are structural cues only; each aerial spin is a single revolution with a landing or a ground beat between revolutions, never a continuous chain; the blade stays the same single straight double-edged jian with a dark hilt from the first frame to the last and is never duplicated, never bent except for the flex in [Shot 4], and never dissolving; in [Shot 4] the blade is allowed and required to flex into a deep bow and then spring back straight. The two camera sides of <Picture 2> and <Picture 3> belong to one single courtyard and simply give the sequence its front and reverse angles, and the one man standing in each of those stills is <Subject 1> himself, one person photographed from two sides, never two men. [Segment-level state lock: STATE LOCKED - SOLO LOCKED, exactly one human being in the frame from the first frame to the last and the courtyard entirely empty behind him; LI XIANG'S OUTFIT LOCKED, red sash SASH LOCKED, flaring with his momentum; ONE SWORD LOCKED, a single straight double-edged jian with a dark hilt, in his hand from the first frame through [Shot 5], falling alone for the single strike in [Shot 6], and back in his one hand in [Shot 7].]
[Shot 1] At 00:00.000, a wide tracking shot on the front side — purpose: the opening aerial flip. Carrying on from the previous segment, Li Xiang drives off the ground into one aerial flip with the sword in one hand, his body opening out in the air. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2> as the front side, the hall and its lantern rows behind him; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution only. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 2] At 00:01.400, a medium shot on the reverse side — purpose: ground-level low sword work, lifting the blade. Coming down out of the flip, he sinks into low ground-level sword work and lifts the blade to gather the next movement. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3> as the reverse side, the hall receding behind him; character <Picture 1>. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 3] At 00:02.600, a medium orbiting shot on the front side — purpose: a second aerial flip. From the lift he goes up into another aerial flip, his body fully extended in the air. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2>; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution, with a landing between this flip and the one before. [Solo lock: one figure in frame; the blade stays in his hand through the revolution.]
[Shot 4] At 00:04.100, an extreme close-up from a ground-skimming low camera — purpose: the signature beat, sword point driven into the paving and the blade flexing into a drawn bow. Coming down out of the flip he drives the blade down and the point bites vertically into the grey stone slab; the frame is tight on the blade and the point, the steel flexing into a deep bow like a fully drawn bowstring, the blade trembling under the load, the point nailed into the stone and not coming out. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; lighting and paving from <Picture 3>; character <Picture 1>. The core of this beat is the deep bow-shaped flex of the blade, the point straight down, the sword never breaking. [Solo lock: only his one hand on the hilt and the one blade in frame; nobody else anywhere.]
[Shot 5] At 00:05.000, a wide low-angle shot on the reverse side — purpose: the blade springs back and catapults him into a twisting aerial flip. With the flex fully loaded, the bowed blade snaps back like a released bowstring and throws him up off the ground, his body twisting into an aerial flip and opening out in the air with the sun blazing through the foliage behind him. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3> as the reverse side, the high right-hand sun behind him; character <Picture 1>. Launched by the blade's rebound, one single twisting revolution, a crisp landing. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
[Shot 6] At 00:06.100, a medium close shot with the camera low and locked on the blade — purpose: the released blade strikes the paving and throws a single spark. The blade has left his hand and drops alone, point-first, into the grey stone paving; the point bites the stone, a single spark jumps at the point of impact, and the blade stands there bright and straight. Nothing holds it: no hand grips it, no hand throws it, no hand steers it, and there is no other person in this courtyard who could be holding it. Motion and blade path follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 2>; character <Picture 1>. One strike only, one single spark, the blade perfectly straight at the moment of impact. [Solo lock: the only thing moving in the frame is this one blade landing in an empty courtyard.]
[Shot 7] At 00:06.400, a wide tracking shot on the reverse side — purpose: continued air work and the closing settle. From the strike he goes up into one more aerial flip and then lands and settles, his robes falling quiet around him. Motion and camera follow <Video 1>; environment <Picture 3>; character <Picture 1>. One single revolution, a crisp landing. [Solo lock: one figure in frame, the courtyard empty behind him.]
